name: Mushroom
lede: Mushroom is a pale greyish brown with a warm pink cast, named plainly for the vegetable.

sections.title: A colour named for a vegetable
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines *mushroom* as a pale shade of brown like the vegetable [1]. Maerz and Paul dated the name to 1892 [2], and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 files the swatch as a light grayish yellowish brown [2]. It is also in the xkcd color survey of 2010 [2].

Baty notes that colour scales are tuned to their subject: the tones called for in describing butterflies differ from those needed for plants, mushrooms or minerals [3]. The name here is much looser, a common comparison, not a scientific term.

sections.title: The swatch
sections.body: The swatch sits close to [[taupe]], [[beige]], [[fawn]] and [[ecru]], and it is a little pinker than [[manila]] [2]. Like all of these, it is a quiet neutral that depends on its surroundings.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color matches 1,036 paintings in the ColorHub archive, about 4.4%, as photographed [4]. Xugu and Maurice Denis use it at several times the usual rate, and it is notable in Nepali paintings [4].
